requirements.canonical: When a reference to an individual string element of a template occurs on the right hand side of an assignment, the result of the reference IS always a template with the content defined by rules a) to j) of clause 15.6.1.
requirements.original: When the reference occurs on the right hand side of an assignment, the result of the reference is always a template with the following content:

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: right hand side reference; referenced template contains a specific value; 0 <= index < number of items
requirements.canonical: When the referenced template is of a binary or character string type to which a specific value is assigned and the index is non-negative and less than the number of items in the specific value, the result of a right hand side reference IS a specific value containing the single referenced element.
requirements.original: a) A specific value containing a single element if the referenced template is of a binary or character string type to which a specific value is assigned and the index in non-negative and less than the number of items in the specific value.

requirements.subject: ent:specific-value
requirements.canonical: The specific value resulting from a right hand side reference to a string template element CAN contain either a single item of the string type (bit, hex, octet or character) or a matching mechanism inside a value such as AnyElement or AnyElementOrNone.
requirements.original: The value can contain either a single item of the string type (bit, hex, octet or character) or a matching mechanism inside a value (such as AnyElement or AnyElementOrNone).

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: right hand side reference; referenced template contains a pattern; 0 <= index < number of items
requirements.canonical: When the referenced template is of a character string type to which a pattern is assigned and the index is non-negative and less than the number of characters and indexable metacharacters in the pattern, the result of a right hand side reference IS a pattern containing the single referenced character or metacharacter.
requirements.original: b) A pattern containing either a single character or a single metacharacter, if the referenced template is of a character sting type to which a pattern is assigned and the index is non-negative and less than the number of characters and indexable metacharacters inside the pattern.

ambiguity.issue: Typo 'character sting type' for 'character string type'.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: right hand side reference; binary string template contains AnyValue
requirements.canonical: When the referenced template is of a binary string type to which AnyValue is assigned, the result of a right hand side reference IS a specific value containing a single AnyElement matching mechanism.
requirements.original: c) A specific value containing a single AnyElement matching mechanism if the referenced template is of a binary string type to which the AnyValue matching mechanism is assigned.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: right hand side reference; binary string template contains AnyValueOrNone
requirements.canonical: When the referenced template is of a binary string type to which AnyValueOrNone is assigned, the result of a right hand side reference IS a specific value containing a single AnyElement matching mechanism with the ifpresent matching attribute attached.
requirements.original: d) A specific value containing a single AnyElement matching mechanism with the ifpresent matching attribute attached to it if the referenced template is of a binary string type to which the AnyValueOrNone matching mechanism is assigned.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: right hand side reference; character string template contains AnyValue
requirements.canonical: When the referenced template is of a character string type and contains AnyValue, the result of a right hand side reference IS a pattern containing a single ? metacharacter.
requirements.original: e) A pattern containing a single ? metacharacter if the referenced template is of a character string type and contains the AnyValue matching mechanism.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: right hand side reference; character string template contains AnyValueOrNone
requirements.canonical: When the referenced template is of a character string type and contains AnyValueOrNone, the result of a right hand side reference IS a pattern containing a single ? metacharacter with the ifpresent matching attribute attached.
requirements.original: f) A pattern containing a single ? metacharacter with the ifpresent matching attribute attached to it if the referenced template is of a character string type and contains the AnyValueOrNone matching mechanism.

ambiguity.issue: Clause 15.6.1 bullet 1 allows AnyValueOrNone in character string templates only on the left hand side, yet rule f) defines a right hand side result for it; it is unclear whether such a reference is allowed.
readings: A right hand side reference to an element of a character string template containing AnyValueOrNone SHALL yield a pattern "?" with ifpresent.
A right hand side reference to an element of a character string template containing AnyValueOrNone SHALL cause an error, and rule f) is unreachable.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: the referenced template contains a length matching attribute
requirements.canonical: If the referenced template contains a length matching attribute, a right hand side reference to an individual string element SHALL be resolved only if the index is less than the maximum allowed length.
requirements.original: g) If the referenced template contains a length matching attribute, the reference shall be resolved only if the referenced element is less than the maximum allowed length.

ambiguity.issue: 'the referenced element is less than the maximum allowed length' means the index of the referenced element.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: the referenced template contains a length matching attribute
requirements.canonical: The result of a right hand side reference to an individual string element of a template with a length matching attribute SHALL NOT contain the length matching attribute.
requirements.original: The result of the reference shall be without the length attribute.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: the referenced template contains the ifpresent matching attribute
requirements.canonical: If the referenced template contains the ifpresent matching attribute, the result of a right hand side reference to an individual string element SHALL contain the ifpresent matching attribute as well.
requirements.original: h) If the referenced template contains the ifpresent matching attribute, the result of the reference shall contain this attribute as well.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: the referenced template has the present restriction, or is an unrestricted mandatory field / field of union, anytype, record of, set of or array
requirements.canonical: If the referenced template has the present restriction, or the referenced field is unrestricted and represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the result of a right hand side reference to an individual string element SHALL have the present restriction.
requirements.original: i) If the referenced template has the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfills the requirements of the present restriction or if the referenced field is unrestricted and represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the result shall have the present restriction.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence is garbled ('..., a matching symbol that fulfills the requirements of the present restriction or if ...'); the fragment about a matching symbol was read as a parenthetical description of the present restriction.
readings: If the referenced template has the present restriction (or the referenced field is an unrestricted mandatory field or a field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array), the result SHALL have the present restriction.

If the referenced template has the present restriction or contains a matching symbol that fulfils the requirements of the present restriction while being unrestricted in a mandatory field or field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the result SHALL have the present restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: the referenced template has the omit restriction
requirements.canonical: If the referenced template has the omit template restriction (value or omit), the result of a right hand side reference to an individual string element SHALL have the value template restriction.
requirements.original: j) If the referenced template has the value or omit restriction, the result shall have the value restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:right-hand-side
requirements.condition: the reference occurs on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When a reference to an individual string element of a template occurs on the left hand side of an assignment, the right hand side of the assignment SHALL contain either a string value, a specific value of a compatible type, or a pattern.
requirements.original: When the reference occurs on the left hand side of an assignment, the right hand side of the assignment shall contain either a string value or specific value of a compatible type or a pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:right-hand-side
requirements.condition: the reference occurs on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: A string value or specific value on the right hand side of an assignment to an individual string element of a template SHALL contain exactly one indexable item (a bit, hex, octet, character or matching mechanism inside a value).
requirements.original: Both string value and specific value shall contain exactly one indexable item (either a bit, hex, octet, character or matching mechanism inside a value).

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; binary string template contains a specific value; 0 <= index < number of items
requirements.canonical: When an item of a binary string template containing a specific value is assigned using a non-negative index less than the number of items in the specific value, the referenced item SHALL be replaced with the item from the right hand side of the assignment.
requirements.original: a) When referencing an item of a binary string template to which a specific value is assigned, if the index is non-negative and less than the number of items in the specific value, the referenced item shall be replaced with the item from the right hand sign of the assignment.

ambiguity.issue: Typo 'right hand sign' for 'right hand side'.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; binary string template contains a specific value; index >= number of items
requirements.canonical: When an item at index n of a binary string template containing a specific value is assigned and n is greater than or equal to the number of items in the specific value, AnyElement matching symbols SHALL first be appended to the specific value as many times as the difference between n and the number of items, and then the item from the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be appended.
requirements.original: b) When referencing an item at the index n of a binary string template to which a specific value is assigned, if the index is greater than or equal to the number of items in the specific value, first as many AnyElement matching symbols shall be appended to the specific value as is the difference between n and the number of items in the specific value and then the item from the right hand side of the assignment shall be appended to the specific value on the left hand side.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; character string template contains a specific value; 0 <= index < length; right hand side is a specific value
requirements.canonical: When an item of a character string template containing a specific value is assigned using a non-negative index less than the length of the specific value and the right hand side contains a specific value, the referenced item SHALL be replaced with the item from the right hand side of the assignment.
requirements.original: c) When referencing an item of a character string template to which a specific value is assigned, if the index is non-negative and less than the length of the specific value and the right hand side contains a specific value, the referenced item shall be replaced with the item from the right hand sign of the assignment.

ambiguity.issue: Typo 'right hand sign' for 'right hand side'.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; character string template contains a specific value; index == length; right hand side is a specific value
requirements.canonical: When an item of a character string template containing a specific value is assigned using an index equal to the length of the specific value and the right hand side contains a specific value, the character from the right hand side SHALL be appended to the specific value.
requirements.original: d) When referencing an item of a character string template to which a specific value is assigned, if the index is equal to the length of the specific value and the right hand side contains a specific value, the character from the right hand side of the assignment shall be appended to the specific value on the left hand side.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; character string template contains a specific value; index > length or right hand side is a pattern
requirements.canonical: When an item of a character string template containing a specific value is assigned using a non-negative index greater than the string length, or the right hand side is a pattern, the specific value SHALL be converted into a pattern that matches precisely the specific value, escaping characters with metacharacter meaning by a backslash.
requirements.original: e) In all other cases of referencing an item of a character string template to which a specific value is assigned using a non-negative index (i.e. the index is greater than the string length or the item on the right hand side of the assignment is a pattern), the specific value shall be converted into a pattern that matches precisely the specific value (i.e. automatically escaping the characters that would otherwise have a metacharacter meaning by prefixing them with a backslash symbol).

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.canonical: After converting the specific value of a character string template into a pattern, the rules for referencing an item of a pattern on the left hand side of an assignment SHALL be applied to assign the right hand side to this pattern.
requirements.original: Then the rules for referencing an item of a pattern on the left hand side of an assignment shall be applied to assign the right hand side of the assignment to this pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.canonical: The pattern modified by an assignment to an item of a converted character string specific value IS assigned to the referenced template.
requirements.original: The modified pattern is then assigned to the referenced template.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; character string template contains a pattern; 0 <= index < number of items
requirements.canonical: When an item of a character string template containing a pattern is assigned using a non-negative index less than the number of items in the pattern, the referenced character or metacharacter SHALL be replaced with the item from the right hand side of the assignment.
requirements.original: f) When referencing an item of a character string template to which a pattern is assigned, if the index is non-negative and less than the number of items in the pattern, the referenced character or metacharacter shall be replaced with the item from the right hand side of the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; character string template contains a pattern; index >= number of items
requirements.canonical: When an item at index n of a character string template containing a pattern is assigned and n is greater than or equal to the number of items in the pattern, ? metacharacters SHALL first be appended to the pattern as many times as the difference between n and the number of items, and then the item from the right hand side SHALL be appended to the pattern.
requirements.original: g) When referencing an item at the index n of a character string template to which a pattern is assigned, if the index is greater than or equal to the number of items in the pattern, first as many ? metacharacters shall be appended to the pattern as is the difference between n and the number of items in the pattern and then the item from the right hand sign of the assignment shall be appended to the pattern.

ambiguity.issue: Typo 'right hand sign' for 'right hand side'.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern
requirements.condition: the right hand side pattern contains more than one item
requirements.canonical: If the right hand side of an assignment to an item of a character string template (rules e), f) and g)) contains a pattern with more than one item, the pattern SHALL be implicitly converted into a single group metacharacter by enclosing it in parentheses before the assignment.
requirements.original: h) If the right hand side of the assignment described in point e), f) and g) contains a pattern with more than one item, this pattern shall be implicitly converted into a single group metacharacter (by enclosing it to parentheses) before the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; binary string template contains AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone; index >= 0
requirements.canonical: When an item of a binary string template containing AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone is assigned using a non-negative index, a binary string of length 0 IS assigned to the referenced template and rule b) IS applied to finish the assignment.
requirements.original: i) When referencing an item of a binary string template to which the AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone matching symbol is assigned using a non-negative index, a binary string with length 0 is assigned to the referenced template and procedures described in the point b are applied to finish the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:ifpresent-attribute
requirements.condition: the binary string template contained AnyValueOrNone
requirements.canonical: After an assignment to an item of a binary string template that contained AnyValueOrNone, the ifpresent matching attribute SHALL be added to the referenced template if it does not already contain it.
requirements.original: Then, if the referenced template contained the AnyValueOrNone matching symbol, the ifpresent matching attribute shall be added to the referenced template if it does not contain it.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element-reference
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; character string template contains AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone; index >= 0
requirements.canonical: When an item of a character string template containing AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone is assigned using a non-negative index, a pattern of length 0 IS assigned to the referenced template and rule g) IS applied to finish the assignment.
requirements.original: j) When referencing an item of a character string template to which the AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone matching symbol is assigned using a non-negative index, a pattern with length 0 is assigned to the referenced template and procedures described in the point g are applied to finish the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:ifpresent-attribute
requirements.condition: the character string template contained AnyValueOrNone
requirements.canonical: After an assignment to an item of a character string template that contained AnyValueOrNone, the ifpresent matching attribute SHALL be added to the referenced template if it does not already contain it.
requirements.original: Then, if the referenced template contained the AnyValueOrNone matching symbol, the ifpresent matching attribute shall be added to the referenced template if it does not contain it.

requirements.subject: ent:length-attribute
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; template has a length matching attribute; index >= maximum length
requirements.canonical: If the referenced template contains a length matching attribute and the index of a left hand side reference is greater than or equal to the maximum allowed length, the maximum allowed length SHALL be changed to the index + 1.
requirements.original: k) If the referenced template contains a length matching attribute and the index is greater or equal to the maximum allowed length, the maximum allowed length shall be changed to the value of the index + 1.

requirements.subject: ent:ifpresent-attribute
requirements.condition: the referenced template contains the ifpresent matching attribute
requirements.canonical: The ifpresent matching attribute of the referenced template IS NOT removed by an assignment to an individual string element.
requirements.original: l) If the referenced template contains the ifpresent matching attribute, the attribute is not removed by the assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error for every reference to an individual string element of a template that is not covered by the rules of clause 15.6.1.
requirements.original: An error shall be issued in all other cases, i.e.:

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if a template referenced by index notation (on either side of an assignment) contains a matching symbol other than those listed in clause 15.6.1, such as omit, a template list or a complemented template list.
requirements.original: If the referenced template (on the left hand side or right hand side) contains any other matching symbol than those listed above, such as Omit, template list or a complemented template list.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if the index used to reference an individual string element of a template is negative.
requirements.original: If the index is a negative number.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if the index used on the right hand side of an assignment is greater than or equal to the maximum allowed length of the referenced template.
requirements.original: If the index is used on the right hand side of an assignment and is greater than or equal to the maximum allowed length.

ambiguity.issue: 'maximum allowed length' presumably refers to the length matching attribute, but the example (v_oct1[10] on a 2-octet specific value without length attribute) treats an index beyond the actual value length as an error too.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if a right hand side index is greater than or equal to the maximum length given by the length matching attribute.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if a right hand side index is greater than or equal to the number of items of the referenced string template (or its maximum length).

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL issue an error if the index is used on the left hand side of an assignment and the right hand side contains a binary string value or specific template with not exactly one indexable item.
requirements.original: If the index is used on the left hand side of an assignment and the right hand side contains a binary string value or specific template with not exactly one indexable item.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template or template variable MAY reference a sub-field inside a template definition using the dot notation.
requirements.original: Both templates and template variables allow referencing sub-fields inside a template definition using the dot notation.

requirements.subject: ent:subfield
requirements.canonical: A field referenced by dot notation in a template CAN be a subfield of a structured field to which a matching mechanism is assigned.
requirements.original: However, the referenced field may be a subfield of a structured field to which a matching mechanism is assigned.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the reference occurs on the right hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: Referencing, on the right hand side of an assignment, a subfield within a structured field to which omit, AnyValueOrNone, a template list or a complemented template list is assigned SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: a) _Omit, AnyValueOrNone, template lists and complemented lists: referencing a subfield within a structured field_ to which Omit, AnyValueOrNone, a template list or a complemented list is assigned, at the right hand side of an assignment, shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:structured-field
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; structured field contains AnyValueOrNone or omit
requirements.canonical: When a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValueOrNone or omit is assigned is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the structured field IS implicitly set to be present.
requirements.original: When referencing a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValueOrNone or omit is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, the structured field is implicitly set to be present, it is expanded recursively up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield.

requirements.subject: ent:structured-field
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; structured field contains AnyValueOrNone or omit
requirements.canonical: When a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValueOrNone or omit is assigned is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the structured field IS expanded recursively up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield.
requirements.original: When referencing a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValueOrNone or omit is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, the structured field is implicitly set to be present, it is expanded recursively up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield.

requirements.subject: ent:structured-field
requirements.canonical: During the expansion of a structured field containing AnyValueOrNone or omit, AnyValue SHALL be assigned to mandatory subfields and AnyValueOrNone SHALL be assigned to optional subfields.
requirements.original: During this expansion an AnyValue shall be assigned to mandatory subfields and AnyValueOrNone shall be assigned to optional subfields.

requirements.subject: ent:subfield
requirements.canonical: After the expansion of a structured field containing AnyValueOrNone or omit, the value or matching mechanism on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced subfield.
requirements.original: After this expansion the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced subfield.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the reference occurs on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: Referencing, on the left hand side of an assignment, a subfield within a structured field to which a template list or a complemented template list is assigned SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: When referencing a subfield within a structured field to which template lists or complemented template lists are assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:subfield
requirements.condition: right hand side reference; structured field contains AnyValue
requirements.canonical: When a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment, AnyValue SHALL be returned for a mandatory subfield and AnyValueOrNone SHALL be returned for an optional subfield.
requirements.original: b) _AnyValue: when referencing a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValue is assigned, at the right_ hand side of an assignment, AnyValue shall be returned for mandatory subfields and AnyValueOrNone shall be returned for optional subfields.

requirements.subject: ent:structured-field
requirements.condition: left hand side reference; structured field contains AnyValue
requirements.canonical: When a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the structured field IS implicitly expanded recursively up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield.
requirements.original: When referencing a subfield within a structured field to which AnyValue is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, the structured field is implicitly expanded recursively up to and including, the depth of the referenced subfield.

requirements.subject: ent:structured-field
requirements.canonical: During the expansion of a structured field containing AnyValue, AnyValue SHALL be assigned to mandatory subfields and AnyValueOrNone SHALL be assigned to optional subfields.
requirements.original: During this expansion an AnyValue shall be assigned to mandatory subfields and _AnyValueOrNone shall be assigned to optional subfields.

requirements.subject: ent:subfield
requirements.canonical: After the expansion of a structured field containing AnyValue, the value or matching mechanism on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced subfield.
requirements.original: After this expansion the value or matching_ mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced subfield.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the structured field has the ifpresent attribute
requirements.canonical: Referencing a subfield within a structured field to which the ifpresent matching attribute is attached SHALL cause an error, irrespective of the value or matching mechanism to which ifpresent is appended.
requirements.original: c) Ifpresent attribute: referencing a subfield within a structured field to which the ifpresent attribute is attached, shall cause an error (irrespective of the value or the matching mechanism to which ifpresent is appended).

ambiguity.issue: 'ifpresent attribute' is used for the 'ifpresent matching attribute'.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the address type value is null
requirements.canonical: Referencing a field of an address type value whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: d) Special value null: referencing a field of an address type, which actual value is null shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template or a template variable MAY reference an element of a record of, set of or array template or field using the index notation.
requirements.original: Both templates and template variables allow referencing elements of a record of, array or set of template or field using the index notation.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism CAN be assigned to the record of, set of or array template or field within which an element is referenced by the index notation.
requirements.original: However, a matching mechanism may be assigned to the template or field within which the element is referenced.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: omit is assigned to the referenced record of, set of or array field
requirements.canonical: Referencing an element within a record of, set of or array field to which `omit` is assigned SHALL follow the rules specified in clause 6.2.3.
requirements.original: a) _Omit: referencing an element within a record of, set of or array field to which omit is assigned shall follow the_ rules specified in clause 6.2.3.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: a template list, complemented list, subset or superset is assigned to the record of or set of template or field
requirements.canonical: Referencing an element within a record of or set of template or field to which a template list, a complemented list, a subset or a superset is assigned SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: b) Template lists, complemented lists, subset and superset: referencing an element within a record of or set of field to which a complemented list, a subset or a superset is assigned, shall cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: The item heading names template lists, but the rule sentence only lists complemented list, subset and superset; Example 1 shows a template list causing the error. Chose the reading that includes template lists.
readings: Referencing an element within a record of or set of template or field to which a template list, a complemented list, a subset or a superset is assigned SHALL cause an error.
Referencing an element within a record of or set of template or field to which a complemented list, a subset or a superset is assigned SHALL cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: AnyValue without length attribute is assigned; reference on the right hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When an element of a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue without a length attribute is assigned is referenced at the right hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL return AnyValue.
requirements.original: c) _AnyValue: when referencing an element of a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is_ assigned (without a length attribute), at the right hand side of an assignment, AnyValue shall be returned.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: a length attribute is attached to the AnyValue
requirements.canonical: If a length attribute is attached to the AnyValue assigned to a record of or set of template or field, the index of an element reference SHALL NOT violate the length attribute.
requirements.original: If a length attribute is attached to the AnyValue, the index of the reference shall not violate the length attribute.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: AnyValue without length attribute is assigned to the record of or set of template or field; reference on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When an element of a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced element.
requirements.original: When referencing an element within a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is assigned (without a length attribute), at the left hand side of an assignment, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element, AnyElement shall be assigned to all elements before the referenced one (if any) and a single AnyElementsOrNone shall be added at the end.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: AnyValue without length attribute is assigned to the record of or set of template or field; reference on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When an element of a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, AnyElement SHALL be assigned to all elements before the referenced element (if any).
requirements.original: When referencing an element within a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is assigned (without a length attribute), at the left hand side of an assignment, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element, AnyElement shall be assigned to all elements before the referenced one (if any) and a single AnyElementsOrNone shall be added at the end.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: AnyValue without length attribute is assigned to the record of or set of template or field; reference on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When an element of a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, a single AnyElementsOrNone SHALL be added at the end of the resulting template or field.
requirements.original: When referencing an element within a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is assigned (without a length attribute), at the left hand side of an assignment, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element, AnyElement shall be assigned to all elements before the referenced one (if any) and a single AnyElementsOrNone shall be added at the end.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.condition: a length attribute is attached to AnyValue; reference on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When a length attribute is attached to the AnyValue and an element is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the length attribute SHALL be conveyed transparently to the new template or field.
requirements.original: When a length attribute is attached to AnyValue, the attribute shall be conveyed to the new template or field transparently.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index of an element reference into a record of or set of template or field to which AnyValue is assigned SHALL NOT violate the type restrictions of the record of or set of type.
requirements.original: The index shall not violate type restrictions in any of the above cases.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: AnyValueOrNone is assigned; reference on the right hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: Referencing an element within a record of, set of or array field to which AnyValueOrNone (with or without a length attribute) is assigned at the right hand side of an assignment SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: d) _AnyValueOrNone: referencing an element within a record of, set of or array field to which AnyValueOrNone_ with or without a length attribute is assigned on the right hand side of an assignment shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: AnyValueOrNone is assigned; reference on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When an element within a record of, set of or array field to which AnyValueOrNone is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the rules for AnyValue (item c) of clause 15.6.3) SHALL apply.
requirements.original: When referencing an element within a record of, set of or array field to which AnyValueOrNone is assigned on the left hand side of an assignment, the rules for AnyValue shall apply (see item c) for more details).

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: the referenced index is inside a permutation
requirements.canonical: Referencing, by its index, an element of a record of template or field that is located inside a permutation SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: e) _Permutation: when referencing an element of a record of template or field, which is located inside a_ permutation (based on its index), this shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.canonical: The record of element indexes covered by a permutation SHALL be determined by the number of elements of the permutation.
requirements.original: Indexes of elements sheltered by a permutation shall be determined based on the number of permutation elements.

ambiguity.issue: "Sheltered" is not a defined term; it is unclear whether the sentence defines which indexes fall inside the permutation, or how the indexes of elements following the permutation are counted. Chose the first reading (Example 4 is consistent with both).
readings: The record of element indexes covered by a permutation SHALL be the consecutive indexes starting at the position of the permutation, one per permutation element.
The indexes of the elements following a permutation SHALL be computed by counting each permutation element as one index.

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.canonical: A permutation that contains AnyElementsOrNone as a permutation element IS considered to cover all record of element indexes from its position onward.
requirements.original: AnyElementsOrNone as a permutation element causes that the permutation shelters all record of element indexes.

ambiguity.issue: "all record of element indexes" can mean every index of the template or every index starting at the permutation position. Chose the second reading.
readings: A permutation containing AnyElementsOrNone covers all record of element indexes from the position of the permutation onward.
A permutation containing AnyElementsOrNone covers all record of element indexes of the template, including those before the permutation.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: the ifpresent attribute is attached to the record of or set of field
requirements.canonical: Referencing an element within a record of or set of field to which the `ifpresent` attribute is attached SHALL cause an error, irrespective of the value or matching mechanism to which `ifpresent` is appended.
requirements.original: f) Ifpresent attribute: referencing an element within a record of or set of field to which the ifpresent attribute is attached, shall cause an error (irrespective of the value or the matching mechanism to which ifpresent is appended).

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: the record of or set of template or field contains AnyElementsOrNone
requirements.canonical: The result of referencing an element of a record of or set of template or field that contains AnyElementsOrNone IS dependent on the position of AnyElementsOrNone, the referenced index and the length attributes attached to AnyElementsOrNone.
requirements.original: g) _AnyElementsOrNone: when referencing an element of a record of or set of template or field that contains_ _AnyElementsOrNone, the result of an operation is dependent on the position of AnyElementsOrNone, the_ referenced index and length attributes attached to AnyElementsOrNone.

requirements.subject: ent:transformed-form
requirements.canonical: When a reference to an element of a record of or set of template containing AnyElementsOrNone is resolved, the transformed form of the template IS used.
requirements.original: When resolving the reference, a transformed form of the record of or set of template is used.

requirements.subject: ent:transformed-form
requirements.canonical: The transformed form of a record of or set of template IS equal to the original template with every AnyElementsOrNone with a length restriction replaced by a sequence of AnyElement symbols whose size is the lower bound of the length restriction.
requirements.original: The transformed form is equal to the original value where all occurrences of AnyElementsOrNone with a length restriction are replaced with a sequence of AnyElements of the same size as the lower bound.

requirements.subject: ent:transformed-form
requirements.condition: the upper bound of the length restriction is greater than the lower bound
requirements.canonical: If the upper bound of the length restriction of an AnyElementsOrNone is greater than its lower bound, the sequence of AnyElement symbols in the transformed form SHALL be followed by a single AnyElementsOrNone symbol with a length restriction.
requirements.original: If the lower bound is greater than the upper bound, the sequence shall be followed by a single AnyElementsOrNone symbol with a length restriction.

ambiguity.issue: The text says "lower bound is greater than the upper bound", which is impossible for a valid length restriction; Example 5 ({1, * length(1..3), 5} becomes {1, ?, * length(0..2), 5}) shows the upper bound greater than the lower bound is meant. Chose the example-consistent reading.
readings: If the upper bound is greater than the lower bound, the AnyElement sequence SHALL be followed by a single AnyElementsOrNone with a length restriction.
If the lower bound is greater than the upper bound, the AnyElement sequence SHALL be followed by a single AnyElementsOrNone with a length restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: The length restriction of the AnyElementsOrNone appended in the transformed form IS a restriction with lower bound zero and upper bound equal to the difference between the upper and lower bound of the original restriction.
requirements.original: The lower bound of this restriction is zero and the upper bound is the difference between the lower and upper bound of the original restriction. If the lower bound is greater than the upper bound, the sequence shall be followed by a single AnyElementsOrNone symbol with a length restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: the actual value of the address type is null
requirements.canonical: Referencing an element of an address type whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: h) Special value null: referencing an element of an address type, which actual value is null shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: reference on the right hand side; all AnyElementsOrNone positions in the transformed form are greater than the referenced position
requirements.canonical: When an element reference is used at the right hand side of an assignment and the positions of all AnyElementsOrNone symbols in the transformed form are greater than the position of the referenced item, the reference IS resolved using the rules of clause 6.2.3.2.
requirements.original: If positions of all AnyElementsOrNone matching symbols in the transformed form are greater than the position of the referenced item, rules from the clause 6.2.3.2 are used for resolving the reference. When the reference is used at the right hand side of the assignment, the following applies:

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: reference on the right hand side; referenced position >= position of an AnyElementsOrNone in the transformed form
requirements.canonical: When an element reference is used at the right hand side of an assignment and the position of the referenced item is greater than or equal to the position of any AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed template, the reference SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: If the position of the referenced item is greater or equal to the position of any AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed template, an error is generated. When the reference is used at the right hand side of the assignment, the following applies:

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: reference on the left hand side; all AnyElementsOrNone positions in the transformed form are greater than the referenced position; referenced item is not a result of transformation
requirements.canonical: When an element reference is used at the left hand side of an assignment, all AnyElementsOrNone positions in the transformed form are greater than the referenced position and the referenced item is not a result of transformation, the value or matching symbol at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL replace the referenced symbol in the original template.
requirements.original: If the referenced item is not a result of transformation, the value or matching symbol at the right hand side of the assignment shall replace the referenced symbol in the original template. When the reference is used at the left hand side of the assignment, the following applies: If positions of all AnyElementsOrNone matching symbols in the transformed form are greater than the position of the referenced item the following rules are used.

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: reference on the left hand side; all AnyElementsOrNone positions in the transformed form are greater than the referenced position; referenced item is a result of transformation
requirements.canonical: When an element reference is used at the left hand side of an assignment, all AnyElementsOrNone positions in the transformed form are greater than the referenced position and the referenced item is a result of transformation, the AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the original template IS replaced with its transformed form and the assignment IS performed afterwards.
requirements.original: If the referenced element was a result of transformation, then the AnyValueOrNone symbol in the original template is replaced with its transformed form and the assignment is performed afterwards. When the reference is used at the left hand side of the assignment, the following applies: If positions of all AnyElementsOrNone matching symbols in the transformed form are greater than the position of the referenced item the following rules are used.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence names the AnyValueOrNone symbol, but the transformation applies to AnyElementsOrNone with a length restriction (see Example 8).

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: reference on the left hand side; referenced position >= position of a non-last AnyElementsOrNone
requirements.canonical: When an element reference is used at the left hand side of an assignment, the position of the referenced item is greater than or equal to the position of an AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed form and that AnyElementsOrNone symbol is not the last element of the template, the reference SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: If the position of the referenced item is greater or equal to the position of any AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed form and this AnyElementsOrNone symbol is not the last element in the template, an error is generated. When the reference is used at the left hand side of the assignment, the following applies:

requirements.subject: ent:element-reference
requirements.condition: reference on the left hand side; referenced position >= position of an AnyElementsOrNone that is the last symbol of the template
requirements.canonical: When an element reference is used at the left hand side of an assignment, the position of the referenced item is greater than or equal to the position of an AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed form and that AnyElementsOrNone is the last symbol of the template, the value or matching symbol at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced element.
requirements.original: If the position of the referenced item is greater or equal to the position of an AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed form and this AnyElementsOrNone is the last symbol in the template, the value or matching symbol at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element. When the reference is used at the left hand side of the assignment, the following applies:

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.condition: reference on the left hand side; referenced position >= position of an AnyElementsOrNone that is the last symbol of the template
requirements.canonical: After the assignment to an element at or beyond a trailing AnyElementsOrNone, the AnyElementsOrNone symbol and all unbound values between it and the referenced symbol SHALL be replaced with AnyElement symbols.
requirements.original: Then the AnyElementsOrNone symbol and all unbound values between it and the referenced symbol shall be replaced with AnyElement symbols. If the position of the referenced item is greater or equal to the position of an AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed form and this AnyElementsOrNone is the last symbol in the template, the value or matching symbol at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.condition: reference on the left hand side; referenced position >= position of an AnyElementsOrNone that is the last symbol of the template; the AnyElementsOrNone had a length restriction
requirements.canonical: If the trailing AnyElementsOrNone symbol had a length restriction, the number of AnyElement symbols added in its place SHALL NOT exceed the upper bound of the length restriction.
requirements.original: If the AnyElementsOrNone symbol had a length restriction, only as many AnyElement symbols can be added as is the value of the upper bound of the restriction. If the position of the referenced item is greater or equal to the position of an AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed form and this AnyElementsOrNone is the last symbol in the template, the value or matching symbol at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.condition: reference on the left hand side; referenced position >= position of an AnyElementsOrNone that is the last symbol of the template
requirements.canonical: As the last step of an assignment to an element at or beyond a trailing AnyElementsOrNone, an AnyElementsOrNone symbol CAN be appended to the end of the template.
requirements.original: As the last step, an AnyElementsOrNone symbol can be appended to the end of the template. If the position of the referenced item is greater or equal to the position of an AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed form and this AnyElementsOrNone is the last symbol in the template, the value or matching symbol at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.condition: reference on the left hand side; referenced position >= position of an AnyElementsOrNone that is the last symbol of the template; the original AnyElementsOrNone had no length restriction
requirements.canonical: If the original trailing AnyElementsOrNone symbol was unrestricted, an AnyElementsOrNone symbol IS always appended to the end of the template after the assignment.
requirements.original: The symbol is always appended if the original AnyElementsOrNone symbol was unrestricted. If the position of the referenced item is greater or equal to the position of an AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed form and this AnyElementsOrNone is the last symbol in the template, the value or matching symbol at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element.

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.condition: reference on the left hand side; referenced position >= position of an AnyElementsOrNone that is the last symbol of the template; the original AnyElementsOrNone had a length restriction
requirements.canonical: If the original trailing AnyElementsOrNone had a length restriction, an AnyElementsOrNone symbol IS appended to the end of the template only if the restriction included items beyond the referenced item.
requirements.original: If the original AnyElementsOrNone had a length restriction, the symbol is appended only if the restriction included items beyond the referenced item. If the position of the referenced item is greater or equal to the position of an AnyElementsOrNone symbol in the transformed form and this AnyElementsOrNone is the last symbol in the template, the value or matching symbol at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.condition: the original AnyElementsOrNone had a length restriction that included items beyond the referenced item
requirements.canonical: The appended AnyElementsOrNone symbol IS given the original length restriction adjusted by the difference between the size of the template before and after the assignment.
requirements.original: In such a case, the appended symbol contains the original length restriction adjusted by the difference between the size of the template before and after assignment. If the original AnyElementsOrNone had a length restriction, the symbol is appended only if the restriction included items beyond the referenced item.

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated how the bounds are adjusted (e.g. whether the lower bound is clamped at zero) nor how the template size is counted. Example 10 ({1, * length(1..5)} with v_roI[2] := 3 gives * length(0..3)) suggests both bounds are reduced by the number of added elements, with the lower bound not below zero.
readings: Both bounds of the original restriction are reduced by the number of elements added by the assignment, with the lower bound not going below zero.
Both bounds are reduced by the difference in the number of template symbols before and after the assignment, which may yield a negative lower bound.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index of an item referenced in a record of or set of template containing AnyElementsOrNone SHALL NOT violate the type restrictions of the record of or set of type.
requirements.original: The index of the referenced item shall not violate type restrictions in any of the above cases.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-template
requirements.canonical: A signature parameter of a signature template SHALL NOT be referenced directly (e.g. using dot notation), except when modifying the signature template.
requirements.original: While signature templates do not allow referencing their parameters directly (e.g. using dot notation), such a reference is possible when modifying a signature template.

requirements.subject: ent:modified-template
requirements.canonical: A modified signature template MAY reference a signature parameter of its parent signature template.
requirements.original: While signature templates do not allow referencing their parameters directly (e.g. using dot notation), such a reference is possible when modifying a signature template.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism CAN be assigned to a signature template as a whole.
requirements.original: However, there can be a matching mechanism assigned to the signature template.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-parameter
requirements.condition: a template list or complemented list is assigned to the signature template; reference on the left hand side
requirements.canonical: Referencing a signature parameter of a signature template to which a template list or a complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: a) Value lists and complemented lists: referencing a parameter of a signature template to which a value list or a complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, shall cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: "Value list" is used where the matching mechanism is called template list in clause B.1.2.1.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-template
requirements.condition: AnyValue is assigned to the signature template; parameter referenced on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When a signature parameter of a signature template to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the signature template IS implicitly expanded to the parameter level.
requirements.original: b) _AnyValue: when referencing a parameter within a signature to which AnyValue is assigned, at the left hand_ side of an assignment, the signature template is implicitly expanded to the parameter level.

ambiguity.issue: "within a signature" is used where the signature template is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-template
requirements.condition: AnyValue is assigned to the signature template; parameter referenced on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: During the implicit expansion of a signature template to which AnyValue is assigned, AnyValue SHALL be assigned to all signature parameters of the template.
requirements.original: During this expansion an AnyValue shall be assigned to all parameters of the template. b) _AnyValue: when referencing a parameter within a signature to which AnyValue is assigned, at the left hand_ side of an assignment, the signature template is implicitly expanded to the parameter level.

requirements.subject: ent:signature-parameter
requirements.condition: AnyValue is assigned to the signature template; parameter referenced on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: After the implicit expansion of the signature template, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced signature parameter.
requirements.original: After this expansion the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced parameter. b) _AnyValue: when referencing a parameter within a signature to which AnyValue is assigned, at the left hand_ side of an assignment, the signature template is implicitly expanded to the parameter level.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template or a template variable MAY reference an alternative inside a union template using the dot notation.
requirements.original: Both templates and template variables allow referencing alternatives inside a union template definition using the dot notation.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A referenced union alternative CAN belong to a template field to which a matching mechanism is assigned.
requirements.original: However, the referenced alternative may belong to template field containing a matching mechanism.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.condition: omit, AnyValueOrNone, template list or complemented list assigned; reference on the right hand side
requirements.canonical: Referencing an alternative of a union template or template field to which `omit`, AnyValueOrNone, a template list or a complemented list is assigned, at the right hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: a) _Omit, AnyValueOrNone, template lists and complemented lists: referencing an alternative of a union template_ or template field to which Omit, AnyValueOrNone, a template list or a complemented list is assigned, at the right hand side of an assignment, shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:union-template
requirements.condition: AnyValueOrNone or omit is assigned to the union template or template field; reference on the left hand side
requirements.canonical: When an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or `omit` is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the template field IS implicitly set to be present.
requirements.original: When referencing an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or Omit is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, the template field is implicitly set to be present and the referenced alternative becomes the chosen one.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.condition: AnyValueOrNone or omit is assigned to the union template or template field; reference on the left hand side
requirements.canonical: When an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or `omit` is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the referenced alternative IS made the chosen alternative.
requirements.original: When referencing an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or Omit is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, the template field is implicitly set to be present and the referenced alternative becomes the chosen one.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.condition: AnyValueOrNone or omit is assigned to the union template or template field; reference on the left hand side; the referenced alternative is not the last element of the dot notation
requirements.canonical: If the referenced alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or `omit` is assigned is not the last element of the dot notation, the rules of clause 15.6.2 for AnyValue SHALL apply recursively for further expansion.
requirements.original: If the referenced alternative is not the last element of the dot notation, rules in clause 15.6.2 valid for AnyValue shall apply recursively for further expansion. When referencing an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or Omit is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, the template field is implicitly set to be present and the referenced alternative becomes the chosen one.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.condition: AnyValueOrNone or omit is assigned to the union template or template field; reference on the left hand side
requirements.canonical: After the expansion of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or `omit` is assigned, the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced subfield.
requirements.original: After this expansion the value or matching mechanism at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced subfield. When referencing an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValueOrNone or Omit is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, the template field is implicitly set to be present and the referenced alternative becomes the chosen one.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.condition: template list or complemented list assigned; reference on the left hand side
requirements.canonical: Referencing an alternative of a union template field to which a template list or a complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Referencing an alternative of a union template field to which template lists or complemented template lists are assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, shall cause an error.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence names only a "union template field", while item a) otherwise covers "union template or template field"; it is unclear whether a union template (not a field) with a template list is also covered.
readings: Referencing an alternative of a union template or union template field to which a template list or complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.

Referencing an alternative of a union template field (but not of a top-level union template) to which a template list or complemented list is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, SHALL cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.condition: AnyValue assigned; reference on the right hand side
requirements.canonical: When an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the right hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL return AnyValue.
requirements.original: b) _AnyValue: when referencing an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValue is_ assigned, at the right hand side of an assignment, AnyValue shall be returned.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.condition: AnyValue assigned to the union template or template field; reference on the left hand side
requirements.canonical: When an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValue is assigned is referenced at the left hand side of an assignment, the referenced alternative IS made the chosen alternative.
requirements.original: When referencing an alternative of a union template or template field to which AnyValue is assigned, at the left hand side of an assignment, the referenced alternative becomes the chosen one.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.condition: AnyValue assigned to the union template or template field; reference on the left hand side; the referenced alternative is not the last element of the dot notation
