requirements.original: **(…): a list of values or templates;**

requirements.subject: ent:complemented-list
requirements.canonical: The `complement (…)` matching mechanism IS the complement of a list of values or templates.
requirements.original: **complement (…): complement of a list of values or templates;**

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.canonical: The AnyValue matching mechanism `?` IS a wildcard that matches any value.
requirements.original: **?: wildcard for any value;**

requirements.subject: ent:any-value-or-none
requirements.canonical: The AnyValueOrNone matching mechanism `*` IS a wildcard that matches any value or no value at all, i.e. a field that is not present.
requirements.original: ***: wildcard for any value or no value at all, i.e. the field is not present;**

requirements.subject: ent:any-value-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyValueOrNone (`*`) CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set type.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: *** can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set types.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value-or-none
requirements.canonical: AnyValueOrNone (`*`) CAN be used for matching optional fields only.
requirements.original: * can** only be used for matching optional fields.

requirements.subject: ent:value-range
requirements.canonical: The range matching mechanism `(lowerBound .. upperBound)` matches integer or float values between and including the lower bound and the upper bound.
requirements.original: **(lowerBound** `..` _upperBound): a range of integer or float values between and including the lower- and upper_ bounds;

readings: The range matching mechanism applies to integer and float values only.
The range matching mechanism applies to integer and float values and, as allowed by table 11, also to character string values.
ambiguity.issue: The description mentions only integer and float values, while table 11 also allows Range for character strings; the second reading is consistent with table 11 and annex B, but the canonical keeps the stated integer/float semantics.

requirements.subject: ent:superset
requirements.canonical: The `superset` matching mechanism matches a value that contains at least all of the listed elements, and possibly more.
requirements.original: **superset: at least all of the elements listed, i.e. possibly more;**

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: The `subset` matching mechanism matches a value that contains at most the listed elements, and possibly fewer.
requirements.original: **subset: at most the elements listed, i.e. possibly less;**

requirements.subject: ent:pattern
requirements.canonical: The `pattern` matching mechanism matches a charstring or universal charstring value that matches the given format.
requirements.original: **pattern: a charstring or universal charstring that matches this format;**

requirements.subject: ent:decmatch
requirements.canonical: The `decmatch` matching mechanism IS used for matching encoded payload fields.
requirements.original: **decmatch: used for matching of encoded payload fields;**

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value-list-matching
requirements.canonical: An EnumValueIdentifier with a list of templates IS used for matching enumerated values with an associated value list.
requirements.original: **EnumValueIdentifier with list of templates: used for matching of enumerated values with associated value** list.

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: The template list, complemented list, `subset` and `superset` matching mechanisms MAY use the elements of a template by means of the `all from` clause.
requirements.original: The matching mechanisms list, complemented list, subset, and superset can use the elements of a template using the all **from clause.**

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: Every template and value used in a matching mechanism used instead of values, including referenced ones such as those within a pattern, SHALL be completely initialized.
requirements.original: b) All templates and values used in the matching mechanisms above (including the referenced ones, e.g. within a pattern) shall be completely initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism of the group of special symbols that can be used inside values characterizes a value set by varying values inside a value.
requirements.original: These matching mechanisms allow to characterize value sets by varying values inside.

requirements.subject: ent:combined-template
requirements.canonical: A template containing a matching mechanism inside a value notation IS called a combined template.
requirements.original: The template containing a matching mechanism inside a value notation syntax is called a combined template.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A special symbol used inside values has one of the syntaxes "?", "*" or `permutation` "(" {(TemplateBody | "?" | "*" | all from TemplateInstance) [","]} ")", each appearing inside a value notation.
requirements.original:
… "?"… |
  … "*"… |
  … permutation "(" { ( TemplateBody | "?" | "*" | all from TemplateInstance )[","] } ")" …

requirements.subject: ent:any-element
requirements.canonical: The AnyElement matching mechanism `?` IS a wildcard that matches any single element in a string, array, `record of` or `set of` value.
requirements.original: **?: wildcard for any single element in a string, array,** `record of` or set of;

requirements.subject: ent:any-elements-or-none
requirements.canonical: The AnyElementsOrNone matching mechanism `*` IS a wildcard that matches any number of consecutive elements in a string, array, `record of` or `set of` value, or no element at all.
requirements.original: ***: wildcard for any number of consecutive elements in a string, array,** `record of or set of, or no` element at all (i.e. an omitted element);

ambiguity.issue: "omitted element" suggests the special value omit, while what is meant is the absence of any element.

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.canonical: The `permutation` matching mechanism matches all of the listed elements in an arbitrary order.
requirements.original: **permutation: all of the elements listed but in an arbitrary order (note, that ? and * are also allowed as** elements of the permutation list and all elements of a template can be added to permutation using the all from clause).

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.canonical: AnyElement (`?`) and AnyElementsOrNone (`*`) MAY be used as elements of a permutation list.
requirements.original: **permutation: all of the elements listed but in an arbitrary order (note, that ? and * are also allowed as** elements of the permutation list and all elements of a template can be added to permutation using the all from clause).

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.canonical: All elements of a template MAY be added to a `permutation` by means of the `all from` clause.
requirements.original: **permutation: all of the elements listed but in an arbitrary order (note, that ? and * are also allowed as** elements of the permutation list and all elements of a template can be added to permutation using the all from clause).

requirements.subject: ent:permutation
requirements.canonical: Every template or value used in a `permutation` matching mechanism SHALL be completely initialized.
requirements.original: b) All templates or values used in the permutation matching mechanism shall be completely initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:matching-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A matching mechanism of the group of special symbols which describe attributes of values defines properties of values.
requirements.original: These matching mechanisms define properties of values.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: An attribute matching mechanism has the syntax `length` "(" ConstantExpression [".." (ConstantExpression | infinity)] ")" [`ifpresent`], or `ifpresent` alone.
requirements.original:
length "(" ConstantExpression [ ".." ( ConstantExpression | infinity ) ] ")" [ ifpresent ] | 
  ifpresent

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: The `length` matching attribute restricts the string length of a value of a string type and the number of elements of a `record of`, `set of` or array value.
requirements.original: **length:** restrictions for string length of string types and the number of elements for record of, set of and arrays;

requirements.subject: ent:ifpresent
requirements.canonical: The `ifpresent` matching attribute matches an optional field that is omitted, and applies the matching of the template it is attached to when the optional field is present.
requirements.original: **ifpresent: for matching of optional field values (if not omitted).**

readings: `ifpresent` matches an omitted optional field, and otherwise matches the present value against the template it is attached to.
`ifpresent` is used only for matching present (not omitted) optional field values.
ambiguity.issue: "for matching of optional field values (if not omitted)" does not say what happens with an omitted field; the first reading is chosen as it is consistent with annex B.1.4.2 and NOTE 2.

requirements.subject: ent:ifpresent
requirements.canonical: `ifpresent` CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set type.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: **ifpresent can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set types.** **ifpresent can only be used for matching optional fields.**

requirements.subject: ent:ifpresent
requirements.canonical: `ifpresent` CAN be used for matching optional fields only.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: **ifpresent can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set types.** **ifpresent can only be used for matching optional fields.**

requirements.subject: ent:ifpresent
requirements.canonical: Assigning `ifpresent` to a template that already matches `omit` (i.e. `omit`, an `ifpresent` template or AnyValueOrNone) has no effect, and the resulting template matches the same set of values and `omit` as the original template.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Assigning ifpresent to a template that already matches the special value omit (i.e. it is either omit, an **ifpresent template or AnyValueOrNone) has no effect; the resulting template will match the same set of** values and the special value omit as the template the ifpresent is assigned to.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: Every value used in a `length` matching attribute SHALL be completely initialized.
requirements.original: b) All values used in the length matching attribute shall be completely initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:template-restriction
requirements.canonical: A template restriction IS a restriction of the matching mechanisms that MAY be used with a template.
requirements.original: Template restrictions allow to restrict the matching mechanisms that can be used with a template.

requirements.subject: ent:template-restriction
requirements.canonical: A template restriction MAY be applied to template definitions, template variables, formal template parameters and return template types of functions.
requirements.original: Template restrictions are applicable to template definitions and template variables, formal template parameters, and return template types of functions.

requirements.subject: ent:template-restriction
requirements.canonical: A template restriction MAY be applied equally to message templates and signature templates.
requirements.original: Template restrictions can be applied equally to message and signature templates.

requirements.subject: ent:template-restriction
requirements.canonical: A restricted template type has the syntax `template` "(" ( `omit` | `present` | `value` ) ")" Type.
requirements.original: template "(" ( omit | present | value ) ")" Type

requirements.subject: ent:omit-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: A template with the `omit` restriction SHALL resolve to a specific value or `omit`.
requirements.original: (omit) the template shall resolve to a value matching mechanism (i.e. the fields of it shall resolve to a specific value or omit, and the whole template may also resolve to omit).

ambiguity.issue: The undefined term 'value matching mechanism' is used; the explanation in parentheses shows that a specific value (or omit for the whole template) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: Each field of a template with the `omit` restriction SHALL resolve to a specific value or `omit`.
requirements.original: (omit) ... (i.e. the fields of it shall resolve to a specific value or omit, ...)

requirements.subject: ent:omit-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: A template with the `omit` restriction MAY resolve to `omit` as a whole.
requirements.original: (omit) ... and the whole template may also resolve to omit).

requirements.subject: ent:omit-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: A template with the `omit` restriction CAN be used to define a field of a record or set template.
requirements.original: Such a template can be used to define a field of a record and set template and the latter one could still be used in a send statement.

ambiguity.issue: 'record and set template' means a record template or a set template.

requirements.canonical: A record or set template whose field is defined by a template with the `omit` restriction CAN still be used in a `send` operation.
requirements.original: Such a template can be used to define a field of a record and set template and the latter one could still be used in a send statement.

ambiguity.issue: 'send statement' is used for the send operation; 'record and set template' means record or set template.

requirements.subject: ent:value-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: A template with the `value` restriction SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.original: (value) the template shall resolve to a specific value (i.e. the fields of it shall resolve to a specific value or omit, but the whole template shall not resolve to omit).

requirements.subject: ent:value-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: Each field of a template with the `value` restriction SHALL resolve to a specific value or `omit`.
requirements.original: (value) ... (i.e. the fields of it shall resolve to a specific value or omit, ...)

requirements.subject: ent:value-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: A template with the `value` restriction SHALL NOT resolve to `omit` as a whole.
requirements.original: (value) ... but the whole template shall not resolve to omit).

requirements.subject: ent:value-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: A template with the `value` restriction CAN be used to define a mandatory field of a record or set template.
requirements.original: It can be used to define a mandatory field of a record or set template and the latter one could still be used in a send statement.

requirements.subject: ent:value-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: A record or set template whose mandatory field is defined by a template with the `value` restriction CAN still be used in a `send` operation.
requirements.original: It can be used to define a mandatory field of a record or set template and the latter one could still be used in a send statement.

ambiguity.issue: 'send statement' is used for the send operation.

requirements.subject: ent:present-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: A template with the `present` restriction SHALL NOT resolve as a whole to a matching mechanism that matches `omit`.
requirements.original: (present) the template as a whole shall not resolve to matching mechanisms that match omit (i.e. its fields may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes).

requirements.subject: ent:present-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: A field of a template with the `present` restriction MAY contain any matching mechanism or matching attribute.
requirements.original: (present) ... (i.e. its fields may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes).

requirements.subject: ent:present-restricted-template
requirements.canonical: A template with the `present` restriction CAN be used to define a mandatory field of a record or set template.
requirements.original: Such a template can be used to define a mandatory field of a record or set template.

requirements.subject: ent:template-restriction
requirements.canonical: A template restriction allows a TTCN-3 tool to check more easily at compile time whether templates and matching expressions are used correctly.
requirements.original: NOTE: Template restrictions allow TTCN-3 tools to check more easily at compile time whether templates and matching expressions are used correctly.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: Whether a TTCN-3 tool checks template restrictions at compile time (rejecting invalid code) or at execution time (raising dynamic errors) IS outside the scope of the present document.
requirements.original: Whether the checks are performed at compile time and invalid code is rejected or whether the checks are performed at execution time and dynamic errors are raised, is outside the scope of the present document.

requirements.canonical: If the base template has the `omit` restriction, a modified template SHALL NOT have the `value` or `present` restriction.
requirements.original: Restriction of base template: template(omit); Allowed restrictions of modified template: Yes; Col3: No; Col4: No; Col5: Yes

requirements.subject: ent:modified-template
requirements.condition: the base template has the `value` restriction
requirements.canonical: If the base template has the `value` restriction, a modified template MAY have the `omit`, `value` or `present` restriction or be unrestricted.
requirements.original: Restriction of base template: template(value); Allowed restrictions of modified template: Yes; Col3: Yes; Col4: Yes; Col5: Yes

requirements.subject: ent:modified-template
requirements.condition: the base template has the `present` restriction
requirements.canonical: If the base template has the `present` restriction, a modified template MAY have the `present` restriction or be unrestricted.
requirements.original: Restriction of base template: template(present); Allowed restrictions of modified template: No; Col3: No; Col4: Yes; Col5: Yes

requirements.subject: ent:modified-template
requirements.condition: the base template has the `present` restriction
requirements.canonical: If the base template has the `present` restriction, a modified template SHALL NOT have the `omit` or `value` restriction.
requirements.original: Restriction of base template: template(present); Allowed restrictions of modified template: No; Col3: No; Col4: Yes; Col5: Yes

requirements.subject: ent:modified-template
requirements.condition: the base template is unrestricted
requirements.canonical: If the base template is unrestricted, a modified template MAY be unrestricted.
requirements.original: Restriction of base template: Template; Allowed restrictions of modified template: No; Col3: No; Col4: No; Col5: Yes

requirements.subject: ent:modified-template
requirements.condition: the base template is unrestricted
requirements.canonical: If the base template is unrestricted, a modified template SHALL NOT have the `omit`, `value` or `present` restriction.
requirements.original: Restriction of base template: Template; Allowed restrictions of modified template: No; Col3: No; Col4: No; Col5: Yes

requirements.subject: ent:mandatory-field
requirements.condition: the parent has the `omit` or `value` restriction
requirements.canonical: A mandatory field of a record or set template, an alternative of a union or anytype template, or an element of a record of, set of, array, map or the parameters of a signature template SHALL have the implicit restriction `template(value)` if the parent template, field, alternative or element has the `omit` or `value` restriction.
requirements.original: Referenced field, alternative or element: Mandatory field of a record or set, alternative of an union or anytype, element of a record of, set of, array, map or parameters of a signature template; Restriction of the parent template, field, alternative or element: template (value); Col3: template (value); Col4: template (present); Col5: template (present)

requirements.subject: ent:mandatory-field
requirements.condition: the parent has the `present` restriction or is unrestricted
requirements.canonical: A mandatory field of a record or set template, an alternative of a union or anytype template, or an element of a record of, set of, array, map or the parameters of a signature template SHALL have the implicit restriction `template(present)` if the parent template, field, alternative or element has the `present` restriction or is unrestricted.
requirements.original: Referenced field, alternative or element: Mandatory field of a record or set, ...; Col4: template (present); Col5: template (present)

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.condition: the parent has the `omit` or `value` restriction
requirements.canonical: An optional field of a record or set template SHALL have the implicit restriction `template(omit)` if the parent template, field, alternative or element has the `omit` or `value` restriction.
requirements.original: Referenced field, alternative or element: Optional field of a record or set; Restriction of the parent template, field, alternative or element: template (omit); Col3: template (omit); Col4: template; Col5: template

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.condition: the parent has the `present` restriction or is unrestricted
requirements.canonical: An optional field of a record or set template SHALL be implicitly unrestricted if the parent template, field, alternative or element has the `present` restriction or is unrestricted.
requirements.original: Referenced field, alternative or element: Optional field of a record or set; ... Col4: template; Col5: template

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.canonical: The `match` operation IS the operation that compares a value, specified as an expression, with a template.
requirements.original: The match operation allows to compare a value (specified in form of an expression) with a template.

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.canonical: The `match` operation has the syntax `match` "(" Expression "," TemplateInstance ")".
requirements.original: match "(" Expression "," TemplateInstance ")"

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.canonical: The `match` operation returns a `boolean` value.
requirements.original: The match operation returns a boolean value.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: The expression parameter of the `match` operation SHALL denote a value or a field of a value.
requirements.original: It matches an expression, which shall denote a value or a field of a value against a template instance.

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.canonical: The type of the expression parameter and the type of the template instance parameter of the `match` operation SHALL be compatible.
requirements.original: Types of the expression and the template instance shall be compatible (see clause 6.2.15).

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.canonical: The `match` operation returns `true` if the expression matches the template instance and `false` otherwise.
requirements.original: The return value of the match operation indicates whether the expression matches the specified template instance.

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.canonical: A non-optional value expression MAY be matched with a template instance that matches an omitted field (Omit, AnyValueOrNone or IfPresent).
requirements.original: In the special case, matching a non-optional value expression (e.g. a value variable or non-optional field of a value) with a template instance that matches an omitted field (i.e. one of the matching mechanisms Omit, AnyValueOrNone, _IfPresent) shall be allowed and shall be treated as if the value expression were an optional field.

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.condition: the template instance matches an omitted field and the expression is a non-optional value
requirements.canonical: When a non-optional value expression is matched with a template instance that matches an omitted field, the `match` operation SHALL treat the value expression as if it were a present optional field.
requirements.original: In the special case, matching a non-optional value expression ... shall be treated as if the value expression were an optional field.

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.canonical: The `match` operation SHALL return `false` when a value expression is matched against a template instance that evaluates to the Omit matching mechanism.
requirements.original: Thus, matching a value_ expression against a template instance which evaluates to the omit matching mechanism shall return false.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: The expression parameter of the `match` operation SHALL evaluate to a value or denote an omitted optional field.
requirements.original: a) The expression-parameter of the match operation shall evaluate to a value or shall denote an omitted optional field, i.e. the match operation cannot be used to compare two templates.

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.canonical: The `match` operation SHALL NOT be used to compare two templates.
requirements.original: ... i.e. the match operation cannot be used to compare two templates.

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.canonical: The operands of the `match` operation SHALL be completely initialized.
requirements.original: b) The operands of the match operation shall be completely initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The type of the template instance parameter of the `match` operation SHALL be unambiguously identified.
requirements.original: c) The type of the template instance-parameter shall be unambiguously identified.

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.condition: the expression parameter evaluates to a literal value without explicit or implicit identification of its type
requirements.canonical: If the expression parameter of the `match` operation evaluates to a literal value without explicit or implicit identification of its type, the type of the template instance parameter SHALL be used as the type context of the expression parameter.
requirements.original: If the expression-parameter evaluates to a literal value without explicit or implicit identification of its type, the type of the template instance-parameter shall be used as the type governor for the expression-parameter.

ambiguity.issue: 'type governor' is used instead of the glossary term 'type context'.

requirements.subject: ent:valueof-operation
requirements.canonical: The `valueof` operation IS the operation that returns the value specified within a template.
requirements.original: The valueof operation allows to return the value specified within a template.

requirements.subject: ent:valueof-operation
requirements.canonical: The value returned by the `valueof` operation MAY be assigned to a variable, used in an expression or used as an actual value parameter.
requirements.original: The returned value can be assigned to a variable, may be used in expressions, as an actual value parameter, etc.

ambiguity.issue: The list ends with 'etc.'; reading 1 (any place where a value is allowed) is chosen as the most likely intent.
readings: The value returned by the `valueof` operation MAY be used wherever a value of its type is allowed.
The value returned by the `valueof` operation MAY be assigned to a variable, used in an expression or used as an actual value parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:valueof-operation
requirements.canonical: The `valueof` operation has the syntax `valueof` "(" TemplateInstance ")".
requirements.original: valueof "(" TemplateInstance ")"

requirements.subject: ent:valueof-operation
requirements.canonical: The `valueof` operation returns the value of its template instance parameter.
requirements.original: The valueof operation returns the value of a template instance.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The template instance parameter of the `valueof` operation SHALL be completely initialized.
requirements.original: a) The template shall be completely initialized and resolve to a specific value.

ambiguity.issue: 'template' is used for the template instance parameter of `valueof`.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: The template instance parameter of the `valueof` operation SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.original: a) The template shall be completely initialized and resolve to a specific value.

ambiguity.issue: 'template' is used for the template instance parameter of `valueof`.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A template of a string type or list type (`bitstring`, `octetstring`, `hexstring`, `charstring`, `universal charstring`, `record of`, `set of` or array) MAY be concatenated from several single in-line templates using the concatenation operation.
requirements.original: Templates of string and list types (bitstring, octetstring, hexstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of, and array) can be concatenated from several single (in-line) templates using the concatenation operation.

requirements.subject: ent:single-template
requirements.condition: the concatenated templates are not of charstring or universal charstring type
requirements.canonical: Each single template of a template concatenation, except for templates of `charstring` and `universal charstring` types, SHALL have the same root type.
requirements.original: With the exception of charstring and universal charstring templates, each single template shall have the same root type.

requirements.subject: ent:single-template
requirements.canonical: A single template of a binary string type in a template concatenation SHALL evaluate only to a specific value, a combined template, AnyValue without a length modifier, or AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone constrained to a fixed length.
requirements.original: The single templates of binary string types shall evaluate only to the matching mechanisms specific value, combined template, AnyValue without a length modifier, AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone, both constrained to a fixed length.

readings: The term 'combined template' denotes a template that is itself the result of a template concatenation.
The term 'combined template' denotes any template composed of several matching mechanisms (e.g. a specific value containing matching symbols inside).
ambiguity.issue: The term 'combined template' is not defined in clause 3.1 nor elsewhere in clause 15; the first reading (result of a previous concatenation) is assumed.

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operation
requirements.canonical: The concatenation of templates of binary string types IS the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right.
requirements.original: The concatenation of templates of binary string types results in the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right, with two exceptions: matching symbol AnyValue without a length modifier shall be replaced by a single AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol before concatenation and matching symbols AnyValue and _AnyValueOrNone that are each constrained to a fixed length N shall be replaced by N AnyElement matching symbols_ before concatenation.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.condition: templates of binary string types are concatenated
requirements.canonical: When concatenating templates of binary string types, an AnyValue matching symbol without a length modifier SHALL be replaced by a single AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol before concatenation.
requirements.original: The concatenation of templates of binary string types results in the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right, with two exceptions: matching symbol AnyValue without a length modifier shall be replaced by a single AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol before concatenation and matching symbols AnyValue and _AnyValueOrNone that are each constrained to a fixed length N shall be replaced by N AnyElement matching symbols_ before concatenation.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.condition: templates of binary string types are concatenated
requirements.canonical: When concatenating templates of binary string types, an AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone matching symbol constrained to a fixed length N SHALL be replaced by N AnyElement matching symbols before concatenation.
requirements.original: The concatenation of templates of binary string types results in the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right, with two exceptions: matching symbol AnyValue without a length modifier shall be replaced by a single AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol before concatenation and matching symbols AnyValue and _AnyValueOrNone that are each constrained to a fixed length N shall be replaced by N AnyElement matching symbols_ before concatenation.

requirements.subject: ent:single-template
requirements.canonical: A single template of a list type in a template concatenation SHALL evaluate only to a specific value, a combined template, AnyValue with or without a length modifier, or AnyValueOrNone with a length modifier.
requirements.original: The single templates of list types shall evaluate only to the matching mechanisms specific value, combined template, _AnyValue with or without a length modifier, AnyValueOrNone with a length modifier._

readings: The term 'combined template' denotes a template that is itself the result of a template concatenation.
The term 'combined template' denotes any template composed of several matching mechanisms (e.g. a specific value containing matching symbols inside).
ambiguity.issue: The term 'combined template' is not defined in clause 3.1 nor elsewhere in clause 15; the first reading (result of a previous concatenation) is assumed.

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operation
requirements.canonical: The concatenation of templates of list types IS the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right.
requirements.original: The concatenation of templates of list types results in the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right, with two exceptions: before concatenation, an AnyValue matching symbol without a length modifier shall be replaced by a single AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol and AnyValue and AnyValueOrNone matching symbols with a length modifier shall be replaced by an AnyElementsOrNone matching mechanism with the same length modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.condition: templates of list types are concatenated
requirements.canonical: When concatenating templates of list types, an AnyValue matching symbol without a length modifier SHALL be replaced by a single AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol before concatenation.
requirements.original: The concatenation of templates of list types results in the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right, with two exceptions: before concatenation, an AnyValue matching symbol without a length modifier shall be replaced by a single AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol and AnyValue and AnyValueOrNone matching symbols with a length modifier shall be replaced by an AnyElementsOrNone matching mechanism with the same length modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.condition: templates of list types are concatenated
requirements.canonical: When concatenating templates of list types, an AnyValue or AnyValueOrNone matching symbol with a length modifier SHALL be replaced by an AnyElementsOrNone matching mechanism with the same length modifier before concatenation.
requirements.original: The concatenation of templates of list types results in the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right, with two exceptions: before concatenation, an AnyValue matching symbol without a length modifier shall be replaced by a single AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol and AnyValue and AnyValueOrNone matching symbols with a length modifier shall be replaced by an AnyElementsOrNone matching mechanism with the same length modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:single-template
requirements.canonical: A single template of `charstring` or `universal charstring` type in a template concatenation SHALL evaluate only to a specific value, AnyValue with or without a length modifier, AnyValueOrNone with a length modifier, or a pattern.
requirements.original: Single templates of charstring and universal charstring types shall evaluate only to specific values, AnyValue with or without a length modifier, AnyValueOrNone with a length modifier or pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:single-template
requirements.condition: templates of character string types are concatenated
requirements.canonical: When concatenating templates of `charstring` and `universal charstring` types, each single template SHALL be of the `charstring` or the `universal charstring` type.
requirements.original: When concatenating templates of charstring and universal charstring types, each single template shall be either of the charstring or universal charstring type.

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operation
requirements.condition: templates of both charstring and universal charstring type are present in the concatenation
requirements.canonical: When templates of `charstring` and `universal charstring` type are both present in a concatenation, each `charstring` value IS implicitly converted to a `universal charstring` value according to clause 6.3.1 before concatenation.
requirements.original: When templates of charstring and universal charstring type are both present in the concatenation, the charstring values are implicitly converted to universal charstring values according to the rules specified in clause 6.3.1 before concatenation and the resulting template is of the universal charstring type.

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operation
requirements.condition: templates of both charstring and universal charstring type are present in the concatenation
requirements.canonical: When templates of `charstring` and `universal charstring` type are both present in a concatenation, the resulting template IS of the `universal charstring` type.
requirements.original: When templates of charstring and universal charstring type are both present in the concatenation, the charstring values are implicitly converted to universal charstring values according to the rules specified in clause 6.3.1 before concatenation and the resulting template is of the universal charstring type.

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operation
requirements.canonical: The concatenation of templates of character string types IS the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right.
requirements.original: The concatenation of templates of character string types results in the sequential concatenation of the single templates from left to right.

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operation
requirements.condition: all operands are specific values
requirements.canonical: If all operands of a character string template concatenation are specific values, the result of the concatenation IS a specific value.
requirements.original: In case all operands are specific values, the result of concatenation will be a specific value.

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operation
requirements.condition: not all operands are specific values
requirements.canonical: If not all operands of a character string template concatenation are specific values, the result of the concatenation IS a pattern, if possible.
requirements.original: In all other cases, if possible, a pattern will be produced.

readings: If a pattern cannot be produced from the operands, the concatenation SHALL cause an error.
If a pattern cannot be produced from the operands, the concatenation produces some other (non-pattern) template.
ambiguity.issue: 'if possible' does not state when producing a pattern is impossible nor what the result is in that case; given the operand restrictions of 15.11-s007 and table 14, the first reading (error) is assumed.

requirements.subject: ent:single-template
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from the concatenation
requirements.canonical: When producing a pattern from a character string template concatenation, each single template IS first transformed to a character string according to table 14.
requirements.original: When producing the pattern, the templates are first transformed to a character string according to table 14.

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operation
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from the concatenation
requirements.canonical: When producing a pattern from a character string template concatenation, the pattern IS created from the concatenation of the transformed strings.
requirements.original: In the next step, the strings are concatenated and a pattern is created from the concatenation result.

requirements.subject: ent:single-template
requirements.condition: one of the single templates is a pattern with the @nocase modifier
requirements.canonical: If one of the single templates of a character string template concatenation is a pattern with the `@nocase` modifier, all other single templates SHALL also be patterns with the `@nocase` modifier.
requirements.original: If one of the single templates is a pattern with the @nocase modifier, then all other single templates shall also be patterns with the @nocase modifier and the resulting pattern will also have the @nocase modifier.

readings: If one single template is a `@nocase` pattern, every other operand SHALL be a `@nocase` pattern; specific values and AnyValue/AnyValueOrNone operands are not allowed.
If one single template is a `@nocase` pattern, every other operand that is a pattern SHALL also have the `@nocase` modifier; non-pattern operands remain allowed.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the rule excludes non-pattern operands (specific values, AnyValue) from a concatenation with a @nocase pattern; the literal first reading is assumed.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern
requirements.condition: one of the single templates is a pattern with the @nocase modifier
requirements.canonical: If one of the single templates of a character string template concatenation is a pattern with the `@nocase` modifier, the resulting pattern IS also with the `@nocase` modifier.
requirements.original: If one of the single templates is a pattern with the @nocase modifier, then all other single templates shall also be patterns with the @nocase modifier and the resulting pattern will also have the @nocase modifier.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern-definition
requirements.canonical: Concatenation of character strings in a pattern definition IS taking precedence over concatenation of templates.
requirements.original: Concatenation of character strings in a pattern definition always takes precedence over concatenation of templates.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern-definition
requirements.condition: a pattern definition is to be concatenated with a following character string according to the template concatenation rules
requirements.canonical: If a pattern definition is to be concatenated with a following character string according to the template concatenation rules, the pattern definition SHALL be enclosed in parentheses.
requirements.original: If it is necessary to concatenate a pattern definition with a following character string according to the template concatenation rules (thus automatically escaping the string), the pattern definition shall be enclosed into parentheses.

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operation
requirements.canonical: A template concatenation SHALL be performed completely before the resulting template is used (e.g. for assignment or matching).
requirements.original: The concatenation shall be performed completely before using the resulting template (e.g. for assignment or matching) and the result shall be type-compatible with the place of its use.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: The template resulting from a template concatenation SHALL be type-compatible with the place of its use.
requirements.original: The concatenation shall be performed completely before using the resulting template (e.g. for assignment or matching) and the result shall be type-compatible with the place of its use.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: A length matching attribute SHALL NOT directly follow a template or template field produced by concatenation.
requirements.original: The length matching attribute shall not follow a template or template field produced by concatenation directly, but in this case the concatenation shall be placed within a pair of parentheses.

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operation
requirements.condition: a length matching attribute is applied to the concatenation result
requirements.canonical: If a length matching attribute is applied to a template or template field produced by concatenation, the concatenation SHALL be placed within a pair of parentheses.
requirements.original: The length matching attribute shall not follow a template or template field produced by concatenation directly, but in this case the concatenation shall be placed within a pair of parentheses.

requirements.subject: ent:static-rule
requirements.canonical: The general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 SHALL apply to template concatenation in addition to the restrictions of clause 15.11.
requirements.original: In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: Every operand of the concatenation operation SHALL be at least partially initialized.
requirements.original: a) All operands of the concatenation operation shall be at least partially initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:specific-value
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from a character string template concatenation
requirements.canonical: A specific value operand (character string) of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the character string escaped by inserting the "\" character before each of the characters "#", "(", ")", "*", "+", "-", "?", "[", "\", "]", "^", "{", "|", "}".
requirements.original: Concatenation operand: Specific values (character strings); Transformed string: The character string is escaped by inserting the "\" character before each of the following characters: "#", "(", ")", "*", "+", "-", "?", "[", "\", "]", "^", "{", "|", "}".

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from a character string template concatenation
requirements.canonical: An operand `?`, `? length(0..infinity)` or `* length(0..infinity)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "*".
requirements.original: Concatenation operand: ?, ? length(0..infinity) or * length(0..infinity); Transformed string: *

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from a character string template concatenation
requirements.canonical: An operand `? length(0)` or `* length(0)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the empty string.
requirements.original: Concatenation operand: ? length(0) or * length(0); Transformed string: empty string

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from a character string template concatenation
requirements.canonical: An operand `? length(1)` or `* length(1)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "?".
requirements.original: Concatenation operand: ? length(1) or * length(1); Transformed string: "?"

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from a character string template concatenation
requirements.canonical: An operand `? length(1 .. infinity)` or `* length(1 .. infinity)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "?+".
requirements.original: Concatenation operand: ? length(1 .. infinity) or * length(1 .. infinity); Transformed string: "?+"

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from a character string template concatenation
requirements.canonical: An operand `? length(n)` or `* length(n)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "?#(n)".
requirements.original: Concatenation operand: ? length(n) or * length(n); Transformed string: "?#(n)"

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from a character string template concatenation
requirements.canonical: An operand `? length(n .. infinity)` or `* length(n .. infinity)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "?#(n,)".
requirements.original: Concatenation operand: ? length(n .. infinity) or * length(n .. infinity); Transformed string: "?#(n,)"

requirements.subject: ent:any-value
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from a character string template concatenation
requirements.canonical: An operand `? length(n .. m)` or `* length(n .. m)` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "?#(n,m)".
requirements.original: Concatenation operand: ? length(n .. m) or * length(n .. m); Transformed string: "?#(n,m)"

requirements.subject: ent:pattern
requirements.condition: a pattern is produced from a character string template concatenation
requirements.canonical: An operand `pattern "content"` of a character string template concatenation IS transformed into the string "content".
requirements.original: Concatenation operand: pattern "content"; Transformed string: "content"

requirements.subject: ent:omit-operation
requirements.canonical: The `omit` operation IS an operation that checks whether a template instance fulfils the conditions of the omit template restriction.
requirements.original: The omit operation checks if a template instance fullfils conditions of the omit restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-operation
requirements.canonical: The `omit` operation has the syntax `omit` "(" TemplateInstance ")".
requirements.original: omit "(" TemplateInstance ")"

requirements.subject: ent:omit-operation
requirements.condition: the operand fulfils the conditions of the omit template restriction
requirements.canonical: If the operand fulfils the conditions of the omit template restriction (clause 15.8), the `omit` operation IS returning a template with the omit restriction and with the same content as the operand.
requirements.original: A template with the omit restriction and with the same content as the operand, if the operand fulfils conditions of the omit template restriction as described in clause 15.8.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-operation
requirements.condition: the operand does not fulfil the conditions of the omit template restriction
requirements.canonical: If the operand does not fulfil the conditions of the omit template restriction, the `omit` operation SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Any other situation shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: The result of the `omit` operation CAN be safely assigned to a template with the omit restriction.
requirements.original: NOTE: This means that the result of omit(m_myTemplate) can be safely assigned to templates with the omit restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:static-rule
requirements.canonical: The general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 SHALL apply to the `omit` operation.
requirements.original: General static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 apply.

requirements.subject: ent:present-operation
requirements.canonical: The `present` operation IS an operation that checks whether a template instance fulfils the conditions of the present template restriction.
requirements.original: The present operation checks if a template fullfils conditions of the present restriction.

ambiguity.issue: The operand is a TemplateInstance according to the syntax (and clause 15.12 says 'template instance'), but the sentence says 'template'.

requirements.subject: ent:present-operation
requirements.canonical: The `present` operation has the syntax `present` "(" TemplateInstance ")".
requirements.original: present "(" TemplateInstance ")"

requirements.subject: ent:present-operation
requirements.condition: the operand fulfils the conditions of the present template restriction
requirements.canonical: If the operand fulfils the conditions of the present template restriction (clause 15.8), the `present` operation IS returning a template with the present restriction and with the same content as the operand.
requirements.original: A template with the present restriction and with the same content as the operand, if the operand fulfils conditions of the present template restriction as described in clause 15.8.

requirements.subject: ent:present-operation
requirements.condition: the operand does not fulfil the conditions of the present template restriction
requirements.canonical: If the operand does not fulfil the conditions of the present template restriction, the `present` operation SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Any other situation shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: The result of the `present` operation CAN be safely assigned to a template with the present restriction.
requirements.original: NOTE: This means that the result of present(m_myTemplate) can be safely assigned to templates with the present restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:static-rule
requirements.canonical: The general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 SHALL apply to the `present` operation.
requirements.original: General static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 apply.

requirements.subject: ent:presentness-conversion
requirements.canonical: The presentness conversion IS the application of the `.present` notation to a general (unrestricted) template, converting it to a template with the present restriction.
requirements.original: The conversion of a general (unrestricted) template to a template with the present restriction can be achieved by applying the .present notation to the template.

requirements.subject: ent:presentness-conversion
requirements.canonical: The presentness conversion has the syntax TemplateInstance "." `present`.
requirements.original: TemplateInstance "." present

requirements.subject: ent:presentness-conversion
requirements.condition: the template expression has no template restriction
requirements.canonical: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with no template restriction IS yielding a template with the present restriction.
requirements.original: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with no restriction yields a template with the present restriction with the following content:

requirements.subject: ent:presentness-conversion
requirements.condition: the referenced unrestricted template contains AnyValueOrNone
requirements.canonical: If the unrestricted template referenced by the presentness conversion contains AnyValueOrNone, the presentness conversion IS yielding AnyValue.
requirements.original: _AnyValue if the referenced template contained AnyValueOrNone._

readings: If the referenced template is AnyValueOrNone at its top level, the presentness conversion yields AnyValue.
Every AnyValueOrNone contained anywhere in the referenced template (including nested fields) is replaced by AnyValue.
ambiguity.issue: 'contained' does not state whether only the top-level matching mechanism or also nested fields are affected; the top-level reading is assumed, consistent with the present restriction applying to the top level only (clause 15.8).

requirements.subject: ent:presentness-conversion
requirements.condition: the referenced template has the ifpresent attribute attached
requirements.canonical: If the matching mechanism of the unrestricted template referenced by the presentness conversion has the `ifpresent` attribute attached, the presentness conversion IS yielding the same matching mechanism without the `ifpresent` attribute.
requirements.original: Matching mechanism without the ifpresent attribute if the referenced template had this attribute attached to it.

requirements.subject: ent:presentness-conversion
requirements.condition: the referenced template is a template list
requirements.canonical: If the unrestricted template referenced by the presentness conversion is a template list, the presentness conversion IS yielding the template list with all alternatives that evaluate to `omit` removed and with the presentness conversion applied to all other alternatives.
requirements.original: _TemplateList where all the alternatives that evaluate to omit are removed and the presentness conversion is_ applied to all other alternatives.

requirements.subject: ent:presentness-conversion
requirements.condition: none of the other conversion cases applies
requirements.canonical: In all cases other than AnyValueOrNone, a matching mechanism with `ifpresent` and a template list, the presentness conversion of an unrestricted template IS yielding the unchanged template.
requirements.original: Unchanged template in all other cases.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: A matching attribute other than `ifpresent`, such as a length restriction, IS NOT affected by the presentness conversion (e.g. `* length(2..10)` is converted to `? length(2..10)`).
requirements.original: NOTE: Other matching attributes such as length are unaffected by the conversion, e.g. * length(2..10) would be converted to ? length(2..10)

requirements.subject: ent:presentness-conversion
requirements.condition: the template expression has the present or value restriction
requirements.canonical: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with the present or value restriction IS yielding the same template with the same template restriction.
requirements.original: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression that has the present or value restriction yields the same template with the same template restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:presentness-conversion
requirements.condition: the template expression has the omit restriction
requirements.canonical: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with the omit template restriction IS yielding the same template with the value restriction.
requirements.original: Applying the presentness conversion to a template expression with the omit template restriction yields the same template with the value restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:presentness-conversion
requirements.condition: the template only matches omit
requirements.canonical: Applying the presentness conversion to a template that only matches the special value `omit` SHALL result in an error.
requirements.original: a) Applying the presentness conversion to a template that only matches the special value omit shall result in an error.

requirements.subject: ent:value-extraction
requirements.canonical: The value extraction IS the application of the `.value` notation to a template instance, extracting the underlying value from a `charstring` pattern matching mechanism or from a template with the omit restriction.
requirements.original: The extraction of the underlying value from a charstring pattern matching mechanism or a template with the omit restriction can be achieved with the .value notation applied to a TemplateInstance.

readings: The value extraction applies only to `charstring` patterns and to templates with the omit restriction.

The value extraction applies to any template instance that contains a pattern, a value with `ifpresent`, or a value (as stated in the Semantic Description and Restrictions), irrespective of its template restriction.
ambiguity.issue: The introductory sentence limits the operand to charstring patterns and omit-restricted templates, while 15.15-s005..s008 and the example (an unrestricted var template with ifpresent) accept any template containing a value; the broader second reading is assumed in the other requirements, the first is used here as stated.

requirements.subject: ent:value-extraction
requirements.canonical: The value extraction has the syntax TemplateInstance "." `value`.
requirements.original: TemplateInstance "." value

requirements.subject: ent:value-extraction
requirements.condition: the operand is a pattern of the form pattern StringValue
requirements.canonical: Applying the value extraction to a pattern matching mechanism of the form `pattern` StringValue IS yielding the value StringValue.
requirements.original: Applying this extraction to a pattern matching mechanism of the form pattern _StringValue will yield the value_ _StringValue.

requirements.subject: ent:value-extraction
requirements.condition: the pattern contains a matching attribute
requirements.canonical: If the pattern operand of the value extraction contains any matching attribute, the value extraction SHALL remove that attribute.
requirements.original: If the pattern contains any matching attribute, the attribute shall be removed by the extraction._

requirements.subject: ent:value-extraction
requirements.condition: the template evaluates to Value ifpresent
requirements.canonical: Applying the value extraction to a template that evaluates to Value `ifpresent` IS yielding the value Value.
requirements.original: Applying this extraction to a template that evaluates to Value `ifpresent will yield the value Value.`

requirements.subject: ent:value-extraction
requirements.condition: the template contains a value
requirements.canonical: Applying the value extraction to a template that contains a value IS yielding that value.
requirements.original: Applying this extraction to a template that contains a value will yield that value.

requirements.subject: ent:value-extraction
requirements.condition: the template contains neither a pattern, nor a value with ifpresent, nor a value
requirements.canonical: Applying the value extraction to a template that contains neither a pattern, nor a value template with an `ifpresent` matching attribute, nor a value SHALL result in an error.
requirements.original: a) Applying the value extraction to a template that contains neither a pattern nor a value template with an ifpresent matching attribute nor a value shall result in an error.
